mechanism_narrative: RETAIL_REC has improved by 6.9 percentage points from t-2w to t-0w, signaling an ongoing recovery trend. This momentum will persist over the next four weeks, driving RETAIL_REC higher than the baseline mean of the last 28 days.
evidence_refs: fact:RETAIL_REC improved from -48.9 to -41.9 over three weeks
failure_condition: Mean RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is lower than or equal to the mean over the last 28 days.

mechanism_narrative: TRANSIT mobility has stabilized near -40% over the past two weeks after declining sharply. When transit stabilizes above -45%, commuters resume regular transit-dependent retail trips, lifting RETAIL_REC within one week.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT rises above -45% and remains stable for one week
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT at -39.7 in t-0w, up from -47.9 in t-2w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not increase within one week of TRANSIT stabilizing above -45%, or TRANSIT falls below -45% again.

mechanism_narrative: WORKPLACES mobility remains depressed at -44.6%, constraining daytime retail activity. If WORKPLACES does not recover by at least 10 percentage points over the next two weeks, RETAIL_REC will decline further due to reduced commuter-driven foot traffic.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES remains below -40% for two consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES at -44.6 in t-0w, unchanged from t-3w
failure_condition: WORKPLACES rises more than 10 percentage points within two weeks, or RETAIL_REC increases despite WORKPLACES stagnation.

mechanism_narrative: PARKS and RETAIL_REC move together as substitutes for indoor activity. When PARKS mobility improves faster than RETAIL_REC over two weeks, consumers shift outdoor preference, suppressing retail recovery. Current PARKS at -7.0 versus RETAIL_REC at -41.9 indicates outdoor substitution is active.
candidate_trigger: PARKS improves by more than 5 percentage points while RETAIL_REC improves by less than 3 percentage points
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS at -7.0, RETAIL_REC at -41.9 in t-0w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC increases by more than 5 percentage points over the next two weeks despite PARKS improving faster, or PARKS does not improve further.

mechanism_narrative: GROCERY_PHARM has stabilized at -14.4%, indicating essential-goods access is maintained. When essential-goods mobility stabilizes, policy constraints on retail are likely easing. This regime shift will allow RETAIL_REC to recover by 8-12 percentage points over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM remains within a 5-point band for two consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM at -14.4 in t-0w, stable from t-1w
failure_condition: GROCERY_PHARM falls below -20% within the next four weeks, or RETAIL_REC does not improve by at least 5 percentage points.

mechanism_narrative: RESIDENTIAL mobility has plateaued at 10.0%, indicating stable home-based activity. When residential mobility stabilizes, it signals policy constraints are fixed. Under fixed constraints, RETAIL_REC will not recover beyond current levels over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL remains between 9.5 and 11.0 for three consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL at 10.0 in t-0w, stable across all four weeks
failure_condition: RESIDENTIAL falls below 8% or rises above 12%, or RETAIL_REC increases by more than 8 percentage points despite residential stability.

mechanism_narrative: TRANSIT and WORKPLACES move together as indicators of commuting resumption. When both improve simultaneously by more than 5 percentage points over two weeks, commuter-driven retail activity accelerates, lifting RETAIL_REC by at least 6 percentage points within the following two weeks.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT and WORKPLACES both improve by more than 5 percentage points week-on-week
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT at -39.7, WORKPLACES at -44.6 in t-0w
failure_condition: TRANSIT and WORKPLACES do not both improve by 5+ percentage points within two weeks, or RETAIL_REC does not increase by at least 6 percentage points in the subsequent two weeks.

mechanism_narrative: RETAIL_REC has recovered 6.9 percentage points over three weeks while remaining at -41.9%, indicating a slow seasonal recovery cycle. This recovery rate of approximately 2.3 percentage points per week will continue, producing a net improvement of 9-10 percentage points over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: RETAIL_REC improves by 2-3 percentage points per week for two consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:RETAIL_REC improved from -48.9 to -41.9 over three weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC improves by fewer than 8 percentage points over the next four weeks, or the weekly improvement rate falls below 1 percentage point per week.
